open: [P05] citizens: agents_for_view() publishes kind = worker-if-employed else citizen, so two of the four drawn roles never appear in a real run. LcnWorldModel already reads an OPTIONAL `role` key on those rows (citizen / worker / porter / soldier) and maps it straight to the figure — one extra key on the dictionary [P05] is already building and a hauler reads as a hauler and a militiaman reads as a militiaman, in a still, at play zoom. The contract is documented at the top of game/view/render/world_model.gd.

INTEGRATOR / game/boot.gd: the blind judge's 'the opening settlement is mirror-symmetric, identical left and right' is about `opening_commands()`, which is boot's and not [P13]'s. I unfolded the [P13] preview settlement's street plan (85% mirrored -> passes) because that is what the frame lab photographs, but the settlement a player actually launches into is still laid out in boot.gd and I could not touch it. It is worth ten minutes: the test that catches it is tests/render/test_preview_world.gd::test_the_street_plan_does_not_fold_in_half and it ports directly.

[P07] combat: snow_widow's .tres still says render_arch = &"swarm". Nothing reads it any more for that id (LcnSpriteFactory.ENEMY_KINDS wins), but the next creature added will inherit the same trap — the field is a fallback, not a drawing, and a creature that ships with only that field ships invisible. tests/render/test_sprites.gd catches it on the next run either way.

THE THING I DID NOT BUILD, and the next real step for 'hour 3 looks like hour 1': boot marks live 26 seconds and are a ring buffer of 420, so they show where the city went RECENTLY. They do not accumulate into the ground. The ground already has five data fields (kind, snow, heat, soot, city presence) and the sixth — a WEAR field written where agents actually walk, decaying over hours — would replace the fake contour 'tracks' in terrain.gdshader (currently two noise contours revealed by building presence, i.e. a path-shaped lie) with the real map of where the population goes, at zero draw cost, deepening across a run. That is the render-side answer to a city that grows into the screen and it is about a day's work in game/view/render/terrain_field.gd + terrain.gdshader.

MIN_AGENT_PX is still 17, i.e. a person is 17 screen pixels at zoom 0.60 (about 1.9x true scale). Four distinct silhouettes and a trail behind each one is what I spent instead of raising it, because raising the floor makes people bigger and everything else the same size. If the next critic still cannot find the population, the lever is that constant and it is one line — but it should be pulled with the frame lab's crowd beat open, because REACH and PLACES will both move and the floors were set against 17.

[P14] vfx: the storm beat HIDES the vfx layers before measuring, on purpose — it grades [P13]'s ground. The two together (spindrift on the ground plus flakes in the air) is the shipping look and nothing measures the combination.

Perf was measured on four cores shared with other agents under llvmpipe. Draw-call counts and pixel grades are load-independent and are the numbers quoted above; the millisecond figures are not, and only the integrator's single-run measurement should be trusted.
